title: Radiation - 123 school
heading: Radiation
intro: All the data you need is in the question. Round to the correct number of digits.

questions.question: Which three types of radiation are released in radioactive decay?

answers.a: Beta radiation, radio waves and gamma radiation
answers.b: Alpha radiation, beta radiation and gamma radiation
answers.c: Alpha radiation, red light and blue light
answers.d: Alpha radiation, infrared radiation and X-rays

questions.question: What does an alpha particle consist of?

answers.b: Two protons and two neutrons (a helium nucleus)

questions.question: What does a beta particle (beta-minus) consist of?
What is gamma radiation?

answers.b: Electromagnetic radiation with a lot of energy

questions.question: Which material already stops alpha radiation?
Which material stops beta radiation?

answers.d: A layer of air a few cm thick

questions.question: Which material is suitable for shielding gamma radiation?
Which type of radiation is the most penetrating?
Which type of radiation has the greatest ionising effect?
What does ionising radiation mean?

answers.d: Radiation that can knock electrons out of atoms or molecules

questions.question: Which radiation is ionising?
Which radiation has the most energy?
What is the unit of activity (number of decays per second)?
What is the unit of radiation dose in the body (a measure of the damage caused by radiation)?
A radioactive source has an activity of 500 Bq. How many atomic nuclei decay per second?
What is the half-life?

answers.a: The time in which the activity doubles
answers.b: The time in which all nuclei have decayed
answers.c: The time in which the radiation stops penetrating
answers.d: The time in which half of the radioactive nuclei have decayed

questions.question: 80 g of a radioactive substance is present. The half-life is 4.0 days. How many grams are left after 12 days?
A source has an activity of 100 Bq. What is the activity after 3 half-lives?
Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5730 years. What percentage of an amount of C-14 is left after 11 460 years?
1/8 of a substance is left. How many half-lives have passed?
Radium-226 (atomic number 88) decays by emitting an alpha particle. What is the atomic number of the daughter nucleus?
Radium-226 (atomic number 88) decays by emitting an alpha particle. What is the mass number of the daughter nucleus?
Carbon-14 (atomic number 6) decays by beta-minus decay to nitrogen (atomic number 7). What happens to the mass number?
What is background radiation?

answers.a: Radiation that is produced only in X-ray photographs
answers.b: Radiation that is always present around us, for example from the ground and from space
answers.d: Radiation that comes only from nuclear power plants

questions.question: What is the difference between irradiation and contamination?

answers.b: In irradiation you are hit by radiation from outside; in contamination there is radioactive material on or in your body
answers.c: With irradiation, radioactive material is in your body; with contamination you are hit from outside
answers.d: Irradiation takes place only with gamma radiation

questions.question: How do you reduce the radiation exposure from a radioactive source? Name the three ways.

answers.a: Increase the distance, stay longer, no shielding
answers.b: Decrease the distance, stay longer, no shielding
answers.c: Increase the distance, use a shorter time, use shielding

questions.question: What do you use to measure radioactive radiation?
What do you use X-rays for in a hospital?

answers.d: To make images of bones and organs

questions.question: Why is nuclear waste dangerous for a long time?

answers.b: Nuclear waste disappears after a day
answers.c: Some substances have a very long half-life and so keep emitting radiation for a long time

questions.question: What happens in nuclear fission?

answers.a: A heavy atomic nucleus splits into smaller nuclei and energy is released
answers.c: Two light nuclei fuse into one heavier nucleus
answers.d: An atom loses only an electron

questions.question: Which radiation does a microwave oven use?
A smoke detector often contains a small source that emits alpha radiation. Why is that not dangerous as long as the detector is intact?

answers.c: Alpha radiation is already stopped by the casing and a thin layer of air

questions.question: Why is an alpha source especially dangerous if the radioactive material gets inside your body?

answers.a: Alpha radiation is very penetrating and goes straight through you
answers.b: Alpha radiation is strongly ionising and is completely absorbed in the body
answers.d: Alpha radiation only heats the skin
